description:

eventMetadata.context_description: The open 2028 Republican presidential nomination field, absent an incumbent, underpins current trader consensus with Robert F. Kennedy Jr. at 49.0 percent. J.D. Vance follows at 30.6 percent, bolstered by his vice presidential role and party visibility, while Marco Rubio stands at 25.4 percent due to his Senate leadership and administration ties. Lower probabilities for figures such as Tucker Carlson and Ron DeSantis reflect their more limited recent positioning within Republican primary dynamics. The broad distribution across dozens of names signals typical early-cycle uncertainty, where future primary schedules, endorsements, and policy alignments could alter these implied probabilities before formal balloting begins.

eventMetadata.context_description: In a wide-open race for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, traders assign the highest implied probability to Gavin Newsom amid a fragmented field where no candidate has consolidated broad support. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Kamala Harris rank next, followed by figures such as Jon Ossoff and Josh Shapiro, reflecting differences in name recognition, fundraising networks, and regional or ideological bases. With the contest still years from the first primaries, probabilities remain sensitive to early endorsements, midterm results, national polling trends among Democratic voters, and any candidate announcements or withdrawals that could narrow the field. Historical patterns show that party elites and primary performance often accelerate consolidation behind viable contenders in similar early-stage cycles.
